As of now, there is limited publicly available detailed information about Marianne Streiff-Feller in widely recognized or English-language sources. She appears to be a relatively private individual or not a major public figure on an international scale.

However, based on available references—primarily from Swiss sources—Marianne Streiff-Feller is known in Switzerland as a politician affiliated with the Swiss People's Party (Schweizerische Volkspartei, SVP/UDC). She has been active in regional or cantonal politics, particularly in the Canton of Bern. She served as a member of the Grand Council of Bern (Grosser Rat des Kantons Bern), which is the cantonal parliament.

Her political focus has reportedly included issues related to education, family policy, and social affairs—common areas of emphasis for many SVP representatives at the cantonal level. She has also been involved in local community and church-related activities, reflecting the intersection of civic and religious engagement typical in some Swiss political circles.

Please note that information about regional Swiss politicians can be sparse in international databases or English-language media, and much of the available detail may be in German or accessible primarily through Swiss local government or party websites.

If you’re looking for specific details—such as her voting record, exact tenure dates, or policy positions—it may be best to consult the official website of the Grand Council of Bern or the Bernese branch of the SVP.
